title: 'Proof' time travel is real with strange item spotted in photo from 1936
excerpt: A 1936 photograph has left conspiracy theorists debating whether time travel is real after a man appears to be holding something unusual
content:
A 1936 photograph has left conspiracy theorists debating whether time travel is real after a man appears to be holding something unusual

08:00, 20 Sep 2026Updated 09:36, 20 Sep 2026

At first glance, this appears to be a photograph capturing an ordinary scene from a New York City street in 1936.

‌

However, people are convinced that one surprising detail confirms the reality of time travel after they spot something unusual in the snap.

‌

The photo captures a street scene in Brooklyn's Union Square but one person in the picture is doing something very out of the ordinary.

‌

The man who is seen in the foreground of the photo looks like he's holding a mobile phone to his ear, a device not available until the 1980s.

This revelation has sent conspiracy theorists into a fact-finding frenzy, with some suggesting that the man in question is a time traveller.

While this could potentially be the case, the man could also be holding something else to his ear, or even just scratching his head.

However, this is not the first time a 'mobile phone' has been spotted in an image which was taken before the handheld device was invented.

‌

Footage from 1938 also supported the theory that 'time travel is real', according to commentators.

In the film clip, a group of people are seen walking towards the camera, with one young woman standing out as she's holding something to the side of her head.

The woman in question is seen chatting as she walks in the crowd of people, with the 'device' clamped to the side of her head with one hand. She then seems to lower it before the film clip ends.

‌

This has prompted conspiracy theorists to question whether the woman was chatting on a mobile phone, or whether she was clutching a different item against her ear.

Theorists subsequently investigated the assertion more thoroughly, with one YouTube account claiming that the woman in the clip was their great-grandmother, and she was indeed using a mobile phone.

‌

According to YouTube user Planetcheck, the portable device is an experimental wireless telephone created by industrial behemoth Dupont at their facility in Leominster, Massachusetts.

"The lady you see is my great-grandmother Gertrude Jones," the user said.

‌

"She was 17 years old. I asked her about this video and she remembers it quite clearly. She says Dupont had a telephone communications section in the factory.

"They were experimenting with wireless telephones. Gertrude and five other women were given these wireless phones to test out for a week.

"Gertrude is talking to one of the scientists holding another wireless phone who is off to her right as she walks by."

In another bewildering image, a 1670 artwork by Dutch artist Pieter de Hooch depicts a charming household scene, with one of the figures grasping what appears to be an iPhone.

The alleged image of an iPhone - painted centuries before the gadgets were initially invented - can be spotted in the grasp of a gentleman positioned on the right side of the picture, according to conspiracy theorists.
